8.0.0.en: 1- O Lord our Lord, how excellent is thy name in all the earth! who hast set thy glory above the heavens.

8.0.1.en: 1- God's glory is wonderful, appearing in all His creation that is on the earth.

8.0.2.en: 2- God's majesty and greatness are above the heavens, for they surpass all creation, earthly and heavenly.

8.0.3.en: 3- The earth signifies the human body, and the wonder appeared in the Incarnation of Christ, which surpasses all understanding, for He is higher than the heavens, which signify the spirits of human beings.

8.0.4.en: 4- God's work shines in the earth, that is, the body of every person, and above the heavens, which are the spirits of human beings; and while God's glory is manifest in all His creation, His glory is magnified in man, with his spirit and his body.

8.0.5.en: 5- The Lord is our Lord, that is, our Lord, we who believe, and He has a special glory in the spirits and bodies of His saints, for they are His children in a special way, so He gave grace to their spirits to cling to Him in prayers, and in their bodies, so they worked miracles, and even after their death the bodies of many of them did not decay.

8.0.6.en: 6- When man feels the love of God, who is glorified in him, he praises Him, and his praises rise above the visible and perceptible heaven, and he joins with the angels in praising God, whose majesty is lifted above the heavens, that is, in the heaven of heavens.

8.1.0.en: 2- Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings hast thou founded praise because of thine adversaries, that thou mightest silence the enemy and the avenger.

8.1.1.en: Adversaries: your enemies, that is, the devils.

8.1.3.en: a- The young in age who gathered around Christ and whom the disciples tried to keep away, but He said, "Suffer little children, and forbid them not, to come unto me" (Mt 19:14). Indeed He praised them, for He asked His followers to become like them, saying, "Except ye be converted, and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven" (Mt 18:3).

8.1.4.en: b- They are the humble, who are like children in their simplicity.

8.1.5.en: c- They are those born of the font of Baptism, that is, the beginner believers, of whom Paul the Apostle said, "I have fed you with milk" (1 Cor 3:1, 2).

8.1.7.en: They are those who suckle from the word of God in the Holy Bible.

8.1.8.en: 3- This praise that rises from human beings silences the evil of the devils and binds them, for they are unable to fight the humble and the simple, and cannot take vengeance on them, because they love God and praise Him, and He protects them. A clear example is the babes in the eyes of people, that is, the disciples, for they were weak in their learning and position, but they believed in God, and He worked through them, and they preached in the whole world and brought many souls to Christ (1 Cor 1:27, 29).

8.2.0.en: 3- When I behold thy heavens, the work of thy fingers, the moon and the stars, which thou hast made;

8.2.1.en: 1- David joins with the babes and sucklings in praising God, and declares that the reason for his praise is the works of God that He created, especially the heavens and what is in them of moon and stars, each of which has its course in which it travels with precision and does not collide with another, lest hard disasters occur.

8.2.2.en: 2- The heavens signify loftiness, that is, the spiritual life that is high above earthly things and lusts, and the moon signifies the Church, and the stars signify the Apostles and the saints and all God's children, and all of them are lit by the light of the sun, which signifies Christ the Sun of Righteousness; therefore he did not mention the sun here, because it points to Christ.

8.2.3.en: 3- God made the heavens with His fingers and all that is in them such as the moon and the stars, and he shows that He made them with precision and also with ease, because precision suits fingers, and he did not say with His hands.

8.2.4.en: 4- The fingers of God signify the work of the Holy Spirit, as Luke the Evangelist expressed it (Lk 11:20). The Holy Spirit is the One who created the heavens and what is in them, and He is the One who raises the spiritual life and works in the Church and the saints, who are symbolized by the moon and the stars.

8.2.5.en: Contemplate the nature around you to see God clearly in it, and He speaks to you about Himself through it, as He spoke to the prophet David and he expressed it in (Ps 19). (2) The dignity of man (vv. 4-8)

8.3.0.en: 4- What is man, that thou art mindful of him? and the son of man, that thou visitest him?

8.3.1.en: 1- David wondered at God's care for man in creating him in His image and likeness, and likewise His providence for him in ordering all his needs. In addition He made him head of all creation; God created it for his sake, to serve him and guard him and help him to reach salvation.

8.3.2.en: 2- David saw God's spiritual care for man in arranging salvation for him after his fall, for He taught him the idea of sacrifice. And He was glorified in godly men, to be an example for mankind, such as Enoch, Noah, Job, Abraham ... then He sent him prophets and gave him commandments and a written Law, to call him to repentance and show him his need for salvation.

8.3.3.en: 3- David saw by the spirit of prophecy the Incarnation of Christ the Son of Man, that is, His condescension in taking the body of a man to visit mankind, then His life among human beings, to be an example for them, and His redemption and resurrection and ascension into heaven, to prepare a place for man and take him up with Him. It is a care and visitation that surpasses understanding.

8.4.0.en: 5- For thou hast made him a little lower than the angels, and crowned him with glory and splendor.

8.4.1.en: 1- God created man with great glory, a little lower than the great angels who are in the heavens, because he has a material body liable to change and death, but if he lives in righteousness and repentance, he will be transformed into a spiritual body united with his spirit and will live forever like the angels. This lack in man is temporary in this life, but in eternity he will be in the glory of the angels.

8.4.2.en: 2- God crowns man with the glory and splendor of the virtues, the good works, and every spiritual relationship with God that he acquires through his life on earth, especially during the tribulations that he bears with thanksgiving.

8.4.3.en: 3- This verse is a clear prophecy about Christ, who condescended by His Incarnation, so that in form He became lower than the angels, but He showed His glory by His resurrection and His ascension into the heavens, and then was crowned with glory and honor, when He prepared a place for His children in heaven, and He, like a slain lamb, stands in their midst, as the Book of Revelation tells us (Rev 5:6), declaring His love poured out for His children.

8.5.0.en: 6- Thou madest him to have dominion over the works of thy hands; thou hast put all things under his feet: 7- All sheep and oxen, yea, and the beasts of the field; 8- The fowl of the air, and the fish of the sea, and whatsoever passeth through the paths of the seas.

8.5.1.en: 1- God alone is the possessor of authority, and He gives it to His creatures such as man.

8.5.2.en: 2- God gave man complete authority over all animals and plants, but he lost this authority by his fall into sin. And when he repented God restored it to him in the New Testament, as the two lions submitted to St. Anthony and dug a grave for St. Paul the Hermit, and as the serpent submitted to St. Barsoum the Naked and lived with him in the cave.

8.5.3.en: 3- Man was able to overcome wild beasts by hunting them with tricks and deceit, or by frightening them, as in the circus, or by killing them using various weapons; this is an incomplete authority, but it is completed if the holiness of this man increases, as in the examples mentioned previously.

8.5.4.en: 4- This authority was given to man in completeness in Paradise, and he regains it partially in proportion to his holiness. But on the other hand these verses speak about Christ, God incarnate, who has complete authority over these creatures, because He is their Creator.

8.5.5.en: 5- The creatures mentioned in these verses have spiritual symbols, which are:

8.5.6.en: Sheep: signify the flock of Christ that is subject to Him; or the Jews who believed in Christ.

8.5.7.en: Oxen: signify the leaders of the Jews who bore the yoke, that is, the responsibility; as it says, "Thou shalt not muzzle the ox that treadeth out the corn" (1 Tim 5:18).

8.5.8.en: Beasts of the field: signify the Gentiles who believed and submitted to Christ, or the distant sinners who repented and returned to God.

8.5.9.en: Fowl of the air: signify the angels and the saints soaring in the heaven of spiritual things.

8.5.10.en: Fish of the sea: signify those who are tossed about amid the lusts of the world, but through their repentance they enjoy the salvation of Christ.

8.5.11.en: 6- There is another reflection on these creatures, which is that the sheep and oxen and beasts signify the body and its lusts, while the fowl of the air signify self, boasting and pride, and finally the fish of the sea signify the circumstances around us that oppose us. Over all these God gave us authority to subdue them by our spiritual will and so enjoy His work in them.

8.5.12.en: If only you would subject your abilities to the love of God and His service, and not be troubled by the multitude of your falls and the wars of the devil; for you are able by the power of God to enjoy with your whole being the God who dwells in you.

8.6.0.en: 9- O Lord our Lord, how excellent is thy name in all the earth!

8.6.1.en: 1- When man sees the grace of God that has been given to him in honoring him and giving him dominion over the various creatures, his heart is moved to thanksgiving and glorifying God, for glory is not for man but for God alone.

8.6.2.en: 2- Thanksgiving and praise are man's life; the Psalm began with them and also ends the Psalm with the same words, for thanksgiving and praise are a life and not merely an event, nor do they have a set time, but are at all times.

8.6.3.en: 3- If God has set man as head of all creation, his basic work that endures is glorifying God, and indeed leading all creation in glorifying Him, as is clear from the Third Hoos, which the Church prays every day in her Midnight Praise.

8.6.4.en: If only you would not forget to glorify God every morning and every evening, for praise is the true life on earth and is the only work in heaven. Taste praise here, that you may have a place among those who praise in heaven.

8.6.5.en: A hymn of victory To the chief Musician. On the death of the Son. A Psalm of David. "I will praise thee, O Lord, with my whole heart" ... (v. 1) Introduction:

8.6.6.en: 1- Its writer: the prophet David, and it was repeated by the chief Musician followed by a group of singers.

8.6.7.en: 2- It is a Psalm of praise and thanksgiving that David said after one of his victories.

8.6.8.en: 3- In the Beirut translation, taken from the Hebrew text (which we have in hand), there are two Psalms numbered 9 and 10, whereas in the Septuagint the two Psalms are joined in one Psalm, the ninth, for the following reasons:

8.6.9.en: a- The two Psalms are written on the letters of the Hebrew alphabet, and the tenth Psalm is an extension and completion of the letters of the alphabet found in the ninth.

8.6.10.en: b- The meaning is connected between the two Psalms, for the ninth Psalm speaks about victory in external wars with enemies, and the tenth Psalm speaks about the internal enemies who wrong the poor.

8.6.11.en: c- The two Psalms speak about the struggle between good and evil.

8.6.12.en: d- The two Psalms speak about tribulations.

8.6.13.en: 4- The title of this Psalm is "on the death of the Son", and this has the following meaning:

8.6.14.en: a- On the death of David's son by Bathsheba, or on the death of Absalom.

8.6.15.en: b- Since it did not specify who the Son is, it may be a prophecy about the only-begotten Son, that is, Christ and His death on the Cross and His redemption of mankind.

8.6.16.en: And in the Septuagint the Psalm is titled, instead of the death of the Son, the mysteries of the Son, that is, the mystery of redemption and all it contains of blessings for mankind.

8.6.17.en: 5- In the Septuagint there is in the title "unto the end", or "to the consummation", and what is meant by it is that this Psalm speaks about the son, that is, the people of God, not only the Jews in the Old Testament but the Christian people who remain sons of God forever in the Kingdom, because they believed in Christ and lived for Him.

8.6.18.en: 6- This Psalm is not found in the Agpeya.

9.0.0.en: 1- I will praise the Lord with my whole heart; I will shew forth all thy marvellous works.

9.0.1.en: 1- Praise and thanksgiving from the whole heart, and this results from David's love for God with his whole heart; thanksgiving has degrees, the highest of which is thanksgiving from the whole heart, for a person can be thankful and at times murmuring, or give thanks seeking more gifts, or give thanks superficially, that is, with coldness and weak feelings of love.

9.0.2.en: 2- It is clear that David is rejoicing because of his victory, and the first thing he felt was to thank God. This is the mind of the Church, that she always begins her prayers, like the prayer of the Divine Liturgy, with the prayer of thanksgiving.

9.0.3.en: 3- As a result of praise and thanksgiving, man longs for others to join with him in giving thanks to God, so he tells them of His wonders, so that they love Him, and then they give Him thanks.

9.0.4.en: 4- Whoever loves God with all his heart does not speak about some of the divine wonders but talks about all the works of God with zeal and power that influence those around him, and does not leave any opportunity without speaking in it about God.

9.1.0.en: 2- I will be glad and rejoice in thee: I will sing praise to thy name, O thou most High.

9.1.1.en: 1- Praise and thanksgiving necessarily produce joy within man and delight in fellowship with God.

9.1.2.en: 2- The man who praises feels the loftiness of God and His elevation above human beings, not only in power but in love and perfection in all attributes, so he increases in zeal for praising Him and singing to Him.

9.1.3.en: 3- Joy in God and praising Him gives man steady feelings of joy, so he continues praising God even within tribulations, and experiences new depths in fellowship with God that he does not see outside tribulations, because God rejoices greatly over the one who praises Him at all times and especially in tribulations, so He pours out on him consolations that cannot be expressed.

9.1.4.en: 4- The joys of the world are temporary and leave within man a sense of deprivation and distress, but joy in God is settled within man and results in greater longings toward God and greater enjoyment of delight and gladness.

9.1.5.en: If only you would get used to thanking God in all your prayers and add to your prayers a portion of the hymns of the Church, to experience new depths in the love of God.

9.2.0.en: 3- When mine enemies are turned back, they shall fall and perish at thy presence.

9.2.1.en: 1- The enemies are the demons, or the wicked who follow the demons in their thinking.

9.2.2.en: 2- At thy presence, that is, before the works of God and His power.

9.2.3.en: 3- Satan's retreat before the face of Christ after He overcame him in the temptation (Mt 4:10); this is the retreat of the enemies backward.

9.2.4.en: 4- And when Peter tried to prevent Christ from accepting suffering and death, to complete redemption, Christ rebuked the thoughts of Satan that were in him by saying, "Get thee behind me, Satan" (Mt 16:23); this too is the retreat of the thoughts of the enemies before Christ.

9.2.5.en: 5- And when the officers of the temple came to arrest Christ in the garden of Gethsemane and He asked them whom they sought, and they said to Him Jesus of Nazareth, He said "I am he"; and they went backward and fell to the ground (Jn 18:6).

9.2.6.en: 6- And when Christ, the second Adam, became incarnate and lived without sin, the first Adam, who fell through his weakness, retreated before Him.

9.2.7.en: 7- When believers hold fast to Christ, Satan fears them and retreats and falls backward before the power of God that is in them.

9.3.0.en: 4- For thou hast maintained my right and my cause; thou satest in the throne judging right.

9.3.1.en: 1- In faith David spoke with God, who saves him from his enemies, and even gives him victory over them, and he thanks Him that He accepted his petition and gave him his right and victory, because he was wronged. God, seated on His throne in heaven as a just judge, gave judgment in favor of David the wronged.

9.3.2.en: 2- David asks on behalf of every believer that God sit on His throne within his heart and judge and pass sentence on evil thoughts and every evil intention and feeling, so that the whole heart is God's and all darkness flees from it.

9.3.3.en: 3- David looks by the spirit of prophecy and speaks in the name of the Church, asking Christ to sit on His seat or His throne, which is the Cross, so He binds Satan and passes judgment to free those who believe in Him, and brings them up from hell to Paradise. He takes Adam and his children, among them David, to enjoy with Him in heaven.

9.3.4.en: 4- David also speaks by the spirit of prophecy about Christ the just Judge, who sits on His seat on the day of judgment and judges for the believers in their cases and their wrongs, and compensates them for everything in the Kingdom, and also passes the sentence of punishment on the wicked in eternal torment.

9.4.0.en: 5- Thou hast rebuked the heathen, thou hast destroyed the wicked, thou hast put out their name for ever and ever. 6- O thou enemy, destructions are come to a perpetual end: and thou hast destroyed cities; their memorial is perished with them.

9.4.1.en: 1- David thanks God, who gave him victory over his enemies, and rebuked them from before him, and destroyed them and caused their memory to cease despite their great power, for God supports the weak and gives them victory, because they are His children who believe in Him.

9.4.2.en: 2- God dwells in the heart of His children and rebukes evil thoughts and destroys Satan, who is the wicked one, and annihilates him, that His children may love Him with all their hearts.

9.4.3.en: 3- David also speaks by the spirit of prophecy about Christ crucified, who bound Satan and rebuked sins by His death on the Cross, and demolished Satan's fortresses and cities, that is, the great evils, and so abolished their authority over man, who believes in Him and lives for Him.

9.4.4.en: 4- These two verses apply to Christ the Judge on the day of judgment, who rebukes the nations, that is, the wicked, and casts them into torment, and destroys Satan the wicked one by casting him into Gehenna, and blots out his name and annihilates him, so he has no place in the Kingdom.

9.4.5.en: 5- God blots out the names of the wicked by their death and destruction, and likewise if man repents and believes in Christ He blots out his old life and gives him a new life, and this happens in the sacrament of Baptism, when the old man dies and a man with a new nature is born. Therefore many take care to give their children new names at Baptism. This change happened with Saul of Tarsus, when he believed in Christ, so he left his former life, and his name was even changed to Paul the Apostle, to live as a servant and apostle of Christ, after having been hostile to the Church.

9.5.0.en: 7- But the Lord shall endure for ever: he hath prepared his throne for judgment. 8- And he shall judge the world in righteousness, he shall minister judgment to the people in uprightness.

9.5.1.en: 1- God remains the Judge, seated on His throne forever, that is, to eternity, so He continues to reward the righteous in the Kingdom with glories rising without end. And on the other side He tortures the wicked with torment rising forever.

9.5.2.en: 2- God judges the world and all the peoples in it with justice and uprightness, so He shows partiality to no one and calls every person to account according to what he received. He judges the Jews according to their Law, and the Gentiles according to their conscience. And every person according to his abilities and circumstances, for the one who knows more is required to give more.

9.5.3.en: 3- God's sitting on the seat of judgment reminds us of the cover of the Ark of God's covenant, which was called the mercy seat, for God's justice is perfect and at the same time His mercy is perfect, because He has mercy on the penitent who return to Him, and receives them in His Kingdom.

9.5.4.en: If God is just, then you must repent, O my soul. Humility draws God's mercies, so He lifts your sins from you, and even supports you on the way of life so that you may enjoy His love forever.

9.6.s.en: (3) The Lord the refuge and Savior

9.6.0.en: 9- The Lord also will be a refuge for the contrite, a refuge in times of trouble. 10- And they that know thy name will put their trust in thee: for thou, Lord, hast not forsaken them that seek thee.

9.6.1.en: 1- God is not only just but a fortress and refuge for those who believe in Him, so He protects them from evil, and although they live in the midst of the wicked world, they are in God's protection and no one can harm them except by His permission.

9.6.2.en: 2- God protects only the humble, but the proud He abandons, because they reject Him and rely on themselves, as the tax collector was accepted, whereas the Pharisee received nothing of God's mercies.

9.6.3.en: 3- God's protection appears clearly in tribulations, where people abandon one another, each one caring for himself, but God remains the tender One, who welcomes His children who take refuge in Him and protects them.

9.6.4.en: 4- God is a refuge for everyone who seeks Him, but those who do not seek Him and do not move toward Him will not find protection, that is, the lazy and the negligent do not enjoy God's protection. But whoever holds fast to the name of God is in safety, as Solomon says, "The name of the Lord is a strong tower: the righteous runneth into it, and is safe" (Prov 18:10).

9.6.5.en: 5- The one who is accustomed to repeating the name of God in prayer and praise finds it easy to rely on God, so he is not shaken before tribulations but takes refuge in Him with complete faith.

9.6.6.en: 6- People in general, and believers in particular, are exposed to various tribulations, but they do not lose their peace, because they have God as a refuge and fortress, and so they rely on Him.

9.6.7.en: 7- The one who takes refuge in a refuge hides in it; so the one who hides and denies himself and shows God is the one who enjoys divine protection.

9.7.0.en: 11- Sing praises to the Lord, which dwelleth in Zion: declare among the peoples his doings. 12- For when he maketh inquisition for blood, he remembereth them: he forgetteth not the cry of the humble.

9.7.1.en: 1- God is long-suffering toward the wicked and allows some of His children to be martyred, so He takes them to Himself and brings them up to heaven, but He requires of the wicked the blood of the righteous, as He required of Cain the blood of his brother Abel, when He said to him, "the voice of thy brother's blood crieth unto me from the ground" (Gen 4:10).

9.7.2.en: 2- God is long-suffering and delays the answering of prayers, but He does not forget or neglect any petition lifted up to Him.

9.7.3.en: 3- Because of God's power and justice and love for His children, His children praise Him in every place and sing to Him.

9.7.4.en: 4- God's children tell the people around them of God's works by means of:

9.7.5.en: a- Their righteous life, which gives light to others and shows God.

9.7.6.en: b- Their conversations with others, which show God in an indirect way.

9.7.7.en: c- When they meet people who suffer from problems they encourage them to take refuge in God.

9.8.0.en: 13- Have mercy upon me, O Lord; consider my trouble which I suffer of them that hate me, thou that liftest me up from the gates of death: 14- That I may shew forth all thy praise in the gates of the daughter of Zion: I will rejoice in thy salvation.

9.8.1.en: 1- David declares that sin humbles man, and the enemy Satan tries not only to humble man but to shed his blood, as in (v. 12), but God's mercy and His looking with compassion upon His children delivers them from the hands of Satan and lifts them from the gates of death, which are sins.

9.8.2.en: 2- David was exposed to death in his war with the enemies, but his reliance on God saved him from their hands, so he is an example of the man who prays, believes in God and relies on Him, who does not fear tribulations.

9.8.3.en: 3- David feels that his basic work, as a believer in God, is to praise Him in His temple that is in Zion, that is, Jerusalem, which signifies the Church in the New Testament, and also the Kingdom of Heaven.

9.8.4.en: 4- This praise lifted up before God makes the believer joyful and a light to the world around him, since everyone knows that the cause of his joy is his relationship with God.

9.8.5.en: Be confident of the power of God that is with you, so that you are not troubled by the wars of the devil or your falls, but hasten to repentance and prayer, and you will find God's mercies and His protection, and He will lift you from every sin.

9.9.0.en: 15- The heathen are sunk down in the pit that they made: in the net which they hid is their own foot taken.

9.9.1.en: David shows that evil is on the heads of the wicked, for while they devise schemes against the righteous they themselves fall into them. If they dig a pit for the righteous they themselves fall into it, and if they cast a net their feet are entangled in it and they cannot escape from it. This verse is a confirmation of what the Psalmist said in (Ps 7:15, 16).

9.10.0.en: 16- The Lord is known; He hath carried out a sharper judgment: the wicked is snared in the work of his own hands. The striking of the strings. Selah.

9.10.1.en: 1- David comments on the verse that shows that the evil of sinners comes upon their heads, so he says that the Lord is "known", and he means known by His justice, for He repays the wicked who wrong the righteous.

9.10.2.en: 2- Sharper: very keen, so it is said "sharper than a two-edged sword"

9.10.3.en: What is meant by a sharper judgment is that God's judgment is severe on the wicked who persist in their evils, so He punishes them not only after their death, but also in their lifetime their evil comes upon their heads.

9.10.4.en: 3- Here he affirms that the wicked is snared in the evil that he prepared for the righteous, that is, he faces divine punishment from the schemes that he devised, as the priests and elders of the Jews devised and sentenced Christ to crucifixion, and when He was crucified and redeemed mankind their evil came upon their heads, that is, the death of Christ condemned them, as it saved the penitent and those who believe in His name.

9.10.5.en: 4- The striking of the strings here means that the strings are struck declaring the severity of God's judgment, followed by a musical pause expressed by the word Selah.

9.11.0.en: 17- The wicked shall return to the abyss, and all the nations that forget God.

9.11.1.en: He states in conclusion that the punishment of the wicked is to be cast into the abyss, that is, eternal torment. Their being cast into eternal torment is a natural extension of their evils, for they lived in the pit of sin far from God, so they finally deserved punishment in the eternal abyss; they return to the abyss in which they lived during their life; death does not have mercy on them, because they rejected God and forgot Him in their lives, and it does not lead them to a better place, but to their natural place far from God.

9.12.0.en: 18- For the needy shall not alway be forgotten: the expectation of the poor shall not perish for ever.

9.12.1.en: 1- Here God's love and care for the weak and the poor and all who suffer injustice or distress appears.

9.12.2.en: 2- God is long-suffering toward the wicked and sometimes does not vindicate the wronged quickly, until their crown is complete, and at the same time the cup of His wrath against the wicked is filled. But He cannot neglect or forget the weak who seek Him; therefore their hope is firm in God.

9.12.3.en: 3- By the poor and wretched he also means the humble, that is, the poor in spirit; these God supports and prepares for them the Kingdom with all its glories, as He said in (Mt 5:3).

9.13.0.en: 19- Arise, O Lord; let not man prevail: let the heathen be judged in thy sight. 20- Put them in fear, O Lord: that the nations may know themselves to be but men. Selah. Prevail: be arrogant.

9.13.1.en: 1- David asks God to answer and arise from His long-suffering to stop the pride of the wicked who are proud because of their authority and their wrongs to the righteous, in order to show God's justice and so that the righteous do not faint and doubt.

9.13.2.en: 2- David urges God to judge the wicked who are far from Him, that is, the Gentiles, and he does not hate the wicked but wants the declaration of God's justice, to establish the righteous.

9.13.3.en: 3- He asks God that the wicked fear, so they know that God has authority over them, and that they are merely men like others, so they do not frighten or threaten others or wrong them.

9.13.4.en: 4- The word Selah calls us to reflect on the power of God and the fear of Him, that we may repent and keep away from evil.

9.13.5.en: Do not persist in evil however easy it is, and do not wrong another in order to give yourself rest; for God the Judge sees everything, so return to Him by repentance lest He terrify you by His power, and have mercy on those around you to receive God's mercies. God rescues the poor "Why standest thou afar off, O Lord?" ... (v. 1) Introduction:

9.13.6.en: 1- The Fathers consider this Psalm an extension of the previous Psalm, indeed it is one with the previous Psalm in the Septuagint, as we mentioned. Consequently its subject is the wronging of the poor and how God rescues them, for it deals with the problems that occur to God's people from within, after he told us in the ninth Psalm about the enemies' wars against God's children, that is, external wars.

9.13.7.en: 2- Since this Psalm is an extension of the previous Psalm, its writer is the prophet David; consequently it has no title in the Holy Bible.

9.13.8.en: 3- This Psalm suits everyone who suffers distress, or the Church when she passes through sufferings and cries out to God her Savior.

9.13.9.en: 4- This Psalm makes clear that evil, or good, springs from the heart, so it must be purified.
